abstract.t: Software agents increasingly select and initiate payments on behalf of people and organizations. Existing agent payment protocols record what a principal authorized and that value moved, but not what information the agent relied on when it chose. This document defines the Agent Decision Commitment (ADC): a salted hash commitment to a decision record that identifies the content the agent provided to the model interface (after any agent-side transformation), the model calls made, and the resulting answer and action. The commitment is carried as a single selectively disclosable claim in an existing payment mandate or payment payload and is, by default, registered with a transparency service before the payment is authorized. The decision record and its content remain with the holder and are disclosed only to dispute participants, who can verify them against the mandate and the transparency service and can inspect the content the agent provided to the model. This document defines the data model, the commitment and anchoring procedures, a disclosure and verification procedure that reports attestation levels rather than verdicts, and bindings to three agent payment protocols and to account-to-account credit transfers. It also defines a witnessed reciprocal exchange by which two parties' agents evidence what passed between them: the receiver signs over the committed bytes, independent witnesses fix the time of each step, a failure to answer by a deadline is recorded, and arbiters resolve stalled exchanges.
